headline: 4 Bittensor SS58 addresses catalogued (subnet owner coldkey, owner hotkey, suggested validator child hotkey, plus Rayon Labs developer identity); no EVM contracts exist — Chutes runs natively on Bittensor Substrate chain as Subnet 64.

findings.text: Bittensor has no EVM block explorer. Bittensor-native explorers (metagraph.sh, tao.app, bittensor.ai/subnets/64) surfaced: subnet owner coldkey 5FRYKhbmfXPDoHdUUDMx27E3HuMvAzwjzFMMq3rNurUhAyS9 and owner hotkey 5CS3g6nVJM6ouns8n9buN9CzFf2C1YDHVcVGRcxoirKs2xbV. Confirmed by three independent sources (metagraph.sh, tao.app, tao.bot).

chutes.ai/docs is the canonical docs site; no 'deployed contracts' page exists. Bittensor is a Substrate chain — there are no smart contracts or EVM addresses. The protocol's on-chain identity is anchored entirely by SS58 hotkeys and coldkeys registered on netuid 64.

No audit links were provided in protocol.audit_links and none were found in GitHub repos or docs. The chutesai GitHub org has no audit-report PDFs or security-review references. Skipped — zero audits to surface.

GitHub org https://github.com/chutesai contains 51 repos. Key repos: chutes-api (validator/API code), chutes-miner (miner Ansible/Helm), chutes (SDK/CLI), fiber, e2ee-proxy. The chutes-api README explicitly documents one suggested child hotkey for lite validators: 5Dt7HZ7Zpw4DppPxFM7Ke3Cm7sDAWhsZXmM5ZAmE7dSVJbcQ. No Foundry broadcast, hardhat-deploy, or addresses.json files found — no EVM deployments exist.

Only one chain: Bittensor (Substrate-based, not EVM). No multi-chain enumeration required. On-chain identity is netuid=64 on the Bittensor Subtensor blockchain. Zero EVM addresses across any supported EVM chain (Ethereum, Base, Arbitrum, etc.).

Not applicable. Bittensor uses a metagraph neuron registry (not EVM factory pattern). Chutes SN64 has 256 neuron slots (237–242 miners + 14–19 validators per observed snapshots), enumerable via btcli/subtensor RPC, not via EVM factory view methods. Cap notice: full metagraph enumeration requires Subtensor RPC calls not supported by defipunkd read API.

Three SS58 identities assigned roles: (1) owner coldkey = treasury/governance controller for netuid 64, actor_class unknown (Bittensor coldkey, not multisig or timelock); (2) owner hotkey = subnet-registered operator identity, actor_class unknown; (3) child hotkey 5Dt7HZ7Zpw4DppPxFM7Ke3Cm7sDAWhsZXmM5ZAmE7dSVJbcQ = suggested lite-validator child key published in chutes-api README.

All three SS58 addresses trace to fetched URLs: owner coldkey and hotkey from metagraph.sh fetch (confirmed also by tao.app and tao.bot search snippets); child hotkey from chutes-api GitHub README fetch. All recorded in admin_addresses.

rationale.verdict: Corpus walked: chutes.ai website, chutes.ai/docs, github.com/chutesai (org + chutes-api repo), metagraph.sh/subnets/64, plus search results from metagraph, tao.app, tao.bot, bittensor.ai, coinmarketcap, coingecko. 3 Bittensor SS58 identities catalogued; 0 EVM contract addresses found (protocol runs natively on Bittensor Substrate chain with no EVM contracts). grade=unknown because defipunkd address_book and on-chain read APIs are EVM-scoped; Bittensor SS58 addresses are not queryable via defipunkd /api/contract/read or /api/safe/owners endpoints.

protocol_metadata.about: Chutes is a decentralized, serverless AI compute platform operating as Subnet 64 on the Bittensor network, developed by Rayon Labs. Users deploy open-source AI models (LLMs, image, video, speech, embedding) as containerized 'chutes' accessible via an OpenAI-compatible API, with optional TEE-protected execution for privacy. GPU miners contribute hardware and serve inference requests, while validators cryptographically verify GPU authenticity via the GraVal middleware, score miners on compute capacity, latency, availability, and reliability, and set on-chain weights that determine TAO token emissions. Billing is pay-per-use based on actual GPU time consumed, with miners rewarded in Bittensor's SN64 alpha token through the dTAO emission mechanism.
